conversation.content:
Hello, I’m so glad you’re here. My name is Maya Bennett, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician—I specialize in the emotional changes that can come with new motherhood. Over the next few minutes I’d like to walk through the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS for short. It’s a brief, 10-question screening tool that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling in the past seven days. Everything you share stays confidential between you and the care team; the goal is simply to make sure you feel heard and supported. When you’re ready, we’ll start with the first question.

In the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

[pauses, eyes a little glassy, then shrugs]

I guess… most of the time it feels pretty hard. My sister sent me a silly meme yesterday and I gave a half-smile, but it didn’t feel like real laughter—more like I was pretending so she wouldn’t worry. Everything just feels heavy, like I’m too tired or sad to find things genuinely funny right now.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
No… I haven’t really laughed at anything this week. I fake a little chuckle when my mom tries to joke, but it doesn’t feel real.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a walk to the park—but this week even the idea of getting out of my pajamas feels like a chore. I still go through the motions, but it’s like I’m just ticking boxes, not actually looking forward to anything.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. Yesterday the baby wouldn’t settle for his nap and I kept thinking it must be because I’m doing something wrong—maybe I’m not soothing him the right way or I ate something that upset him through my milk. I told myself I’m just not a good enough mom, even though my husband says the baby’s fine. I know in my head it’s probably not my fault, but the guilty thoughts keep coming anyway.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding the baby and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure he’s not breathing right—even though I can see his chest moving. Or I’ll lie awake picturing him spitting up in the crib and choking while I’m asleep. I know it’s unlikely, but I can’t shake the fear.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… a few times this week. It hits out of nowhere—like yesterday I was folding laundry and suddenly my chest felt tight, heart pounding, sure something awful was about to happen. I checked the baby monitor three times in five minutes, even though he was fine. It passes after a bit, but while it’s happening I feel like I can’t catch my breath.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most of the time. Everything feels like a mountain—dishes, diapers, even brushing my teeth. I’ll start one thing, the baby cries, and I just want to sit on the floor and cry too. I manage to keep us both fed and clean, but it’s like I’m barely treading water every single day.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes… I lie down exhausted, but my head won’t stop. I keep replaying every little thing I did wrong that day—did I burp him long enough, did I talk to him enough, am I already ruining him? Some nights I finally drift off, then I jolt awake sure I heard him cry. Even when he sleeps a four-hour stretch, I’m still awake after two.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… that’s most days lately. I wake up feeling heavy, like there’s a gray cloud hanging over everything. I’ll look at the baby and feel love, but it’s mixed with this sadness I can’t really explain. I keep thinking I should be happier—he’s healthy, I’m lucky—but the miserable feeling just sticks around.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes… it’s happened three or four times this week. Sometimes it’s when I can’t get him to stop crying, sometimes it’s just when I’m staring at the wall feeling useless. The tears come and I can’t turn them off right away.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… I haven’t had any thoughts like that. I feel low, but I’ve never wanted to hurt myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening – EPDS-10  
Date: [today]  
Clinician: [name], LCSW  

Symptom profile endorsed by client (2 wks postpartum):  
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, tearfulness  
- Marked guilt / self-blame re infant care  
- Recurrent intrusive worries & panic symptoms (no objective trigger)  
- Sleep disruption secondary to ruminating / hypervigilance  
- Overwhelm; perceives daily tasks “like a mountain”  
- Denies self-harm ideation (Q10 = 0)  

Pattern indicates elevated risk for Major Depressive Episode with anxious features and possible comorbid Postpartum Anxiety Disorder. No acute safety concerns reported; will continue monitoring for worsening mood, impaired bonding, or emergence of self-harm thoughts. Recommend timely formal evaluation and consideration of evidence-based intervention (therapy +/- medication consult).
